findings.text: Upheld as advisory. `version_of` (first line of --version, exit code ignored) and `stagedVersion` in src/install/binary.ts:17-18 (exit 0 and the whole trimmed output must be a version) read a staged binary's version by different rules, so the curl script can keep a binary that `install` replaces. The reviewer raised it as advisory and no rubric question makes it a defect: the order itself is held equal by tests/unit/version-order.test.ts.

Upheld as advisory. The production command reads the test-only overrides PUSH_REMOTE and PUSH_ORIGIN, and only GITHUB_ACTIONS switches them off. That works today. Reaching `commitAndPush` with `remote` and `origin` directly would take the overrides out of the command. Raised as advisory.
Lowered to advisory as debt outside the change. The moving action tags and the persisted checkout credentials are lines this diff did not add, and docs/real-use/findings.md already defers them.
Lowered to advisory as debt outside the change. This file is not in the diff. Its direct use of Bun.semver.order is already deferred.

Upheld as advisory. AC-66's only `previous: null` case also passes `atPrevious: "missing"`, so deleting `input.previous === null ||` from decideHold (scripts/release/lib.ts:528) leaves the test green. plan.ts:127 always pairs the two, so the behaviour a caller sees is still held, which is why this is not a defect. A case with `previous: null` and a readable `atPrevious` would put that branch under test.
Upheld as advisory. The `step()` helper creates a mkdtempSync folder on each call and never removes it. The assertions are sound; this is test hygiene only.

Upheld as advisory. gitEnv puts the base64 form of the Basic Authorization header into GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0 without `::add-mask::`. The reviewer shows that no current path prints it: git redacts the header and only stderr reaches the ReleaseError sentences. The exposure needs a future trace or debug re-run, so the finding stays advisory, as raised. Masking the encoded value before the first git call would close it.

Upheld as advisory. The first real dispatch makes all four outside writes at once on a plain tag, after a dry run that tests none of them. The spec states this (spec.md:219, :272) and names its way back, a higher version, so no rollback or dependency is missing from the item's spec or plan. Making the first tag that carries this item an rc under `next` would lower the exposure.

Upheld as advisory. The first npm publish moves unpinned npx and OpenCode users from 0.4.4 straight to the new version, across every store migration since then. The spec's Risks do not name this group's first-hour exposure, but the way back is stated (a higher version, and a backup restore in the runbook). It is an unnamed exposure with a stated rollback, not a missing rollback or dependency, so it stays advisory, as raised. One line in Risks would cover it.

Upheld as advisory. The status line links ADR 0009 as `0009-native-install.md`, but the file is `docs/adr/0009-native-installation.md`. It is a broken citation in a document, not a boundary crossed, so it stays advisory. Fix the link.

Upheld as advisory. CLAUDE.md and ADR 0029 call lib.ts 'pure functions', but it also holds `run`, `summary`/`output` and `command`, which have side effects. The base defines no layer that this crosses, so it is a mismatch between description and code, not a defect. Either split those four out or correct the sentence.

Every job in distribute.yml sets 15. The reviewer raised it as advisory under Q6 consistency, and it does not fail a gate, secret, permission or rollback question.
